text:
Claude Giroux is 38, with more than 1,300 NHL games behind him, and he is still useful in a way that doesn't show up in the box score. He has 12 points in 21 games while playing about 17 minutes a night, a pace right in line with our range for him.

The interesting number is at five-on-five. Ottawa gets 58% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), almost 8 points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey said something similar about last season: 2.1 wins above replacement, 47th of 401 forwards, with opponents getting fewer chances when he played (89th percentile). His finishing is right on his chances, 4 goals on 3.8 expected, so nothing here is borrowed.

This is Ottawa's first season after trading Brady Tkachuk, and Giroux is one of the veterans Ottawa leans on. "When we play our game we know we'll always give ourselves a chance to win," as a TSN headline quoted him. He backed it up with the winner against Pittsburgh on the night Linus Ullmark won his 200th game. Watch his minutes; at his age, how Ottawa manages them is the story.
headline: Giroux, at 38, still tilts the ice
